A related vertical layout strategy for SIMD execution is detailed in a thesis on ray tracing implicit surfaces [S2, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the thesis details a data layout strategy for coherent ray tracing where ray information is stored vertically within a packet to exploit SIMD (SSE) parallelism. It confirms that ray directions are stored as separate arrays of X, Y, Z components (vertical) rather than a single horizontal array, and that hit results are stored in aligned SSE arrays. This directly supports the claim that a related vertical layout strategy for SIMD execution is detailed in the thesis.

It confirms the presence of arrays for 'origin' (cameraCenterX/Y/Z), 'direction' (directionX/Y/Z), 't-range bounds' (near_t/far_t), and a 'mask' (gtMask_Device). It also confirms the data structure is optimized for GPU access with separate contiguous arrays per attribute.

Ray directions are stored as separate arrays of X, Y, Z components (vertical), rather than a single horizontal array of 3-vectors, and arrays are 16-byte-aligned to permit access to a packlet of four rays in a single SSE register [S2, unofficial].

The claim states that ray directions are stored as separate arrays of X, Y, Z components (vertical) rather than a single horizontal array of 3-vectors, and that these arrays are 16-byte-aligned to permit access to a packlet of four rays in a single SSE register. Source [S2] explicitly confirms all these points: 'ray directions are stored as separate arrays of X,Y,Z components, as opposed to a single horizontal array of 3-vectors', 'These vertical arrays are 16-byte-aligned', and this alignment permits 'access a packlet of four rays at a time in a single SSE register'.

The layout consists of base arrays allocated for `totalRays` elements [S1, unofficial].

The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly describes a Structure of Arrays (SoA) memory layout optimized for GPU access. It states that ray properties are stored in separate contiguous arrays per attribute, with each array containing `totalRays` elements. It further details the allocation of specific base arrays (origin, direction, t-range, mask, density, weights) and conditional arrays based on the `graylized` flag, all allocated for `totalRays` elements. This directly supports the claim that the layout consists of base arrays allocated for `totalRays` elements.
